source.title: Catch Composition of Bottom Set Gillnet in Caba, La Union, Philippines
source.provider: Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Biology & Fisheries; authors affiliated with Don Mariano Marcos Memorial State University
source.journal: Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Biology & Fisheries
source.citation: Balneg, J., Boado, J., Cucuyao, M., Empeño, E., & Roque, R. L. (2025). Catch Composition of Bottom Set Gillnet in Caba, La Union, Philippines. Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Biology & Fisheries, 29(4), 2451–2472.
source.accessStatus: Publisher-hosted full article PDF reviewed online on 2026-11-19. The 22-page article was not saved locally. The publisher HTML article page and a clear license policy were not confirmed in the bounded review.
source.reuseStatus: No article-level copyright or reuse license was located in the reviewed PDF, and no publisher policy tied to this article was verified. Do not redistribute its tables, figures, photos or extracted dataset until item-specific terms are established.

scope.studyLocality: Municipal waters of Caba, La Union; the article names coastal Barangays Santiago Sur, Santiago Norte, San Carlos and Wenceslao and says eight specific fishing locations were sampled.
scope.samplingDesign: The authors describe bimonthly sampling at 15-day intervals over six months, selecting bottom-set gillnet operators at random and taking a 12-litre bucket sample from the first haul. Samples were transported to the DMMMSU-SLUC Capture Fisheries Laboratory for morphological, morphometric and meristic examination.
scope.gear: Bottom-set monofilament polyamide gillnet, mesh size No. 8, 100 m long and 2.5 m deep. The methods say 24 units per operator were set for one hour; the CPUE table instead gives an eight-hour soaking duration and 192 panels. Clarify how deployment, soaking duration and effort were defined before reusing any CPUE result.
scope.spatialResolution: The article aggregates species/catch tables for Caba and provides a figure with pinned sampling-site locations across four barangays. No text-readable coordinates or species-by-site matrix was found; these pins do not define municipal-water geometry or legal boundaries.
scope.taxonomicResolution: The article reports 43 Table 1 catch labels and 1,324 individuals. The labels include one crustacean (Portunus sanguinolentus) and one genus-level fish label (Mugil sp.); the article's abstract therefore should not be interpreted as 43 fish species. Species identification used collected samples, fisher interviews and secondary references, with morphometric/meristic examination, but no determination key, identifier crosswalk, voucher catalogue or accession numbers are stated.

reportedTopRelativeAbundance.interpretation: Article-reported catch composition from the sampled bottom-set gillnet and study period only; not ecological abundance or current-presence evidence.

checks.issue: Table 2 gives Trichiurus lepturus 30.82% of catch weight, while the following narrative says 32.82%.
checks.disposition: Unresolved; preserve the tabular and narrative values separately if needed and do not choose one silently.

checks.issue: The paper uses Mene maculate in earlier tables but Mene maculata in Table 6; Lutjanus malabricus appears in the tables; Nemipterus japonicas and Portonus sanguinolentus appear in narrative text while tables use Nemipterus japonicus and Portunus sanguinolentus.
checks.disposition: Retain verbatim source strings pending independent identity checks; do not merge or correct records based on spelling alone.

checks.issue: The methods describe gear set for one hour, but the CPUE table uses an eight-hour soaking duration and 192 panels.
checks.disposition: Effort basis needs author/source clarification before using CPUE values comparatively.

decision.use: A high-priority, dated Caba marine-catch research lead for a separate taxon-name audit and possible source follow-up. Keep catch-by-gear evidence distinct from general habitat occurrence, local abundance and current presence.

limitations: Catch composition is selected by one fishing gear and its mesh/operation; it is not a comprehensive inventory of Caba waters or surrounding marine habitats.
The eight fishing locations are aggregated in the tables, and individual taxon rows are not linked to the four named barangays or to map pins.
No voucher, museum accession, sample identifier, field coordinate table, identification key or independent taxonomic verification was found in the reviewed article.
Several source taxon strings, family labels, and narrative percentages conflict internally; the reported 43 rows include a crab and a genus-level fish label.
The deployment/soak effort wording is unresolved. CPUE and relative catch share must not be presented as ecological abundance, population trend, catchability advice or a prediction of likely catch.
No article-specific reuse terms were verified. Do not reproduce or redistribute the species tables, figures, map or photographs based on publisher availability alone.
nextAction: The separate taxon-name review proposes bounded catalog crosswalks while preserving the article strings; seek the authors' voucher/sample accession and coordinate-by-station crosswalk, clarify gear effort, and confirm article reuse rights before considering any candidate species assertion.
